talkTrack.60s:
TALK TRACK · 60 SECONDS

Meridian Commerce Group runs on three systems that never talked: a PostgreSQL warehouse database, cold-chain IoT sensors streaming through Kafka, and Salesforce. Seven data-quality nightmares cost them $127M a year.

The fix is efficiency by design. Two declarative Qlik Cloud Pipelines — version-controlled YAML, imported through the API — land every feed in the Open Lakehouse: Iceberg tables on S3, bronze to silver to gold. Eight transformation routes canonicalize six carrier vocabularies, standardize units, and score trust. Talend validates and geocodes every Salesforce address on a 15-minute cycle, routing the unfixable to Stewardship.

Two governed data products serve the business — read straight from the lakehouse through Amazon Athena, no copies. On top: two analytics apps whose sheets are authored by an AI agent over MCP, Predict models for exceedance and late-delivery risk, Answers grounded on 25 operational documents, and a Discovery Agent watching it all.

One command deploys the whole stack. That's pipelines as code, and AI that actually ships.
talkTrack.2min:
TALK TRACK · 2 MINUTES

Meridian Commerce Group is a global logistics company running commerce across twelve warehouses and six carriers — on three systems that never talked. A PostgreSQL warehouse management database holds inventory, events, and shipments. Cold-chain IoT sensors stream temperature, GPS, and battery telemetry through Kafka, alongside webhook events from six carriers in five languages. Salesforce holds contacts, orders, and the product master. Add 25 operational documents — SOPs, carrier contracts, incident reports — and you have the full picture of where commerce happens. Seven data-quality nightmares across those silos cost MCG $127M a year.

The efficiency story starts with how the data lands. Two declarative Qlik Cloud Pipelines — plain YAML in git, imported and prepared through the platform API — land every feed in the Qlik Open Lakehouse: Apache Iceberg tables on S3, organized bronze, silver, gold. Eight silver transformation routes do the heavy lifting: six carrier status vocabularies collapse into one, units and storage zones standardize, timestamps normalize to UTC per distribution center, and every row carries a trust score. In parallel, Talend pulls Salesforce every fifteen minutes, validates address format in a tMap routine, geocodes the failures against Nominatim, and routes what it can't fix to a Stewardship campaign — human-in-the-loop, closed loop.

The gold layer serves two governed data products — supply chain health and last-mile performance — with datasets attached through the Data Products API and refreshed daily plus on every upstream event. The analytics apps read those products straight from the lakehouse through Amazon Athena. No extracts, no copies, open formats end to end.

On top of that foundation: two analytics apps whose sheets are authored conversationally by an AI agent over the Qlik MCP server, Qlik Predict models trained on lakehouse datasets for temperature-exceedance and late-delivery risk, Qlik Answers grounded on the 25-document knowledge base with cited responses, and a Discovery Agent that finds anomalies before anyone asks. Teams alerts and Talend jobs close the action loop.

The punchline for your buyer: the entire environment — pipelines, products, apps, agents — deploys from one repository with one command, and stays fifteen minutes fresh. That's pipelines as code, governed data products, and AI that actually ships.
